subject: Request: SLA exception & escrowed runbook for Porto Harbor Private VPC
messages:
From: Marta Costa <marta.costa@portoharbor.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Luis Ferreira <luis.ferreira@portoharbor.com>, procurement@portoharbor.com
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Private VPC SLA: request for exception + escrowed runbook

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Porto Harbor is almost finished with the on-site edge rollout (three colo sites + two transit POPs) and we’re ready to move traffic onto the Private VPC. Before we flip the switch we need two things from Redwood so procurement can sign: an explicit operational exception in the SLA for customer-controlled edge components, and a secure escrow of a trimmed runbook that details maintenance procedures for those edge devices.

Specifically we’d like Redwood to: 
- Acknowledge a limited attribution window for availability/latency degradations caused by customer-controlled edge hardware or third-party transit (we propose attributing 40% of latency tail incidents to customer-managed edge for the first 12 months).
- Accept an escrow arrangement where a sanitized runbook (no credentials) is stored with Redwood for incident bridging during scheduled maintenance.
- Define a maintenance notification cadence (48 hours for routine, 1 hour emergency) and an automated telemetry hook (Prometheus exporter or webhook) we can expose for SLA monitoring.

I attached a draft SLA clause and a short runbook excerpt for your review (PH-SLA-draft-v2.pdf, runbook_excerpt.md, network-diagram.png). Procurement is keen to close this week; they asked if we can sign an intent and pilot for 12 months.

If you can point me to the exact language Redwood would need (and any minimum monitoring/telemetry requirements) we’ll get procurement moving.

Best,
Marta Costa
Head of Cloud Ops, Porto Harbor Systems
M: +351 912 345 678

-----Original Attachment Stubs: PH-SLA-draft-v2.pdf (3 pages), runbook_excerpt.md (1.2 KB), network-diagram.png (210 KB)
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Marta Costa <marta.costa@portoharbor.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Private VPC SLA: request for exception + escrowed runbook

Marta —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attachments. We can support an operational exception and an escrowed runbook, but there are a few dependencies and alternatives we need to outline so legal and product can sign off: 

1) Telemetry: we need a stable scrape endpoint or webhook that provides connection-level metrics (latency, packet-loss, interface up/down). Prometheus-compatible is preferred; if you can expose that we’ll hook into Redwood telemetry for alerts.

2) Escrow scope: Redwood will accept a redacted runbook for incident bridging, stored encrypted in our customer vault. We won’t accept credentials or vendor-sensitive automation. We will stipulate a periodic validation test (quarterly smoke test) to confirm handoff viability.

3) Attribution: 40% attribution proposal is non-standard. We can offer a time-bound attribution schedule for a 12-month pilot but legal will want specific incident classes and an appeals process (post-incident RCA with mutually agreed telemetry).

Next steps from our side: I’ve looped Kimberly (legal) for contract language and Laura (ops) for runbook/telemetry feasibility. Kimberly — could you review the attached SLA draft and propose redline language for an "Operational Escrow" amendment? Laura — please confirm the minimum telemetry surface we’d need and whether quarterly smoke tests are operationally feasible from Redwood’s side.

I’m available for a short call tomorrow. Happy to lead a quick sync to unblock procurement.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Strategic Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private VPC SLA: request for exception + escrowed runbook

Sergio,

Thanks for the ping — I reviewed PH-SLA-draft-v2.pdf. High level thoughts: legal will accept an Operational Escrow clause if it contains these items explicitly:

- Definition of Escrowed Artifacts (runbook excerpt only; no automation, no credentials).
- Access conditions: Redwood access only during incident bridging, requires authenticated request from designated on-call and a confirmed RCA ticket.
- Data handling: encrypted at rest (KMS), audit-log retention 7 years for access events.
- Rollback & testing: quarterly simulated handoffs; escrow validity for 12 months with option to renew.
- Attribution matrix: incidents broken into three classes (customer-edge, transit third-party, Redwood-controlled). For the 12-month pilot we can allow a 40% presumption for class B incidents (edge-induced tail latency) but every incident must run the RCA process; attribution presumption can be overturned with telemetry.

I attached a short redline suggestion as a Word doc (redline not physically attached here — will upload to your drive link). Also: legal requires that any attribution percentage be coupled with a minimum remediation timeline (we recommend 48 hours for acknowledgement and 10 business days for initial mitigation plan).

I’ll draft language and share by EOD.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

> On Mon, Jul 24, 2028 at 11:03 Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:46:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Private VPC SLA: request for exception + escrowed runbook

Sergio / Kimberly —

Operational note from the runbook excerpt: we can do the escrow + telemetry hook, but there are two operational paths I want to put on the table for Porto Harbor to consider: 

Option A — Time-bound exception + escrowed runbook (recommended pilot):
- 12-month pilot window.
- Quarterly smoke-handoff test conducted jointly (Redwood on-call + Porto Harbor on-call).
- Redwood provides read-only access to sanitized event streams (latency histograms, interface state).
- Attribution presumption: 40% for class B incidents unless telemetry proves otherwise.
- If telemetry unavailable during incident, default moves to joint investigation and incident is assigned to "undetermined" bucket; service credits handled per standard SLA.

Option B — Fallback during scheduled maintenance (higher cost, more assurance):
- During customer maintenance windows, Redwood will route traffic to a hosted fallback instance for duration of maintenance (additional reserved capacity required).
- This eliminates the need for attribution but will incur incremental monthly costs and requires committed warm standby capacity.

Operational requirements: we need a documented maintenance calendar (CSV feed or calendar-sharing) and a stable telemetry endpoint (Prometheus path + bearer token for scraping). Quarterly tests will require 2-hour windows and an SOW for validation.

I recommend Option A as it’s lowest friction for procurement. If Porto Harbor wants full avoidance of attribution questions, Option B is the path but it’s not our default.

Laura Bennett
Head, Customer Operations (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

Sergio, Kimberly, Laura —

Thanks — Porto Harbor prefers Option A (12-month pilot with quarterly smoke tests and an escrowed redacted runbook). Procurement is ready to sign the intent sheet pending your legal redline and a short SOW for the quarterly handoffs. We attached a signed intent doc (PH-signed-escrow-intent.docx) and we can accept the 48-hour acknowledgement / 10-business-day mitigation timeline Kimberly proposed.

Next items from Porto Harbor:
- Please upload the redlined amendment into the Drive link so procurement can review alongside our counsel.
- Confirm required telemetry endpoints and give us the template for the quarterly smoke test runbook.
- If you can, include a one-paragraph summary of how Redwood will secure escrow access and the audit trail for accesses.

We can do a 30-minute call on Friday morning if that helps.

Best,
Marta Costa
Head of Cloud Ops, Porto Harbor Systems
